items.subject: Grocery: 26 store(s) dropped from a commodity they carry - 2026-08-01
evidence: 21 of 26 gaps are Fareway, 5 are Family Fare. fareway-regular-2026-07-31.json carry_note: '+105 carried ... 196 expired' at the 14-day cap; the 07-27 file expired 0. The expiry removed the old SIZED rows and left the 07-31 storefront-sweep rows, which carry no usable size.

bottled-water | Fareway | 'Fareway Purified Drinking Water' | $3.87 | size='each' | slug '...-fareway-drinking-water-purified-24-each' - a 24-pack whose count exists ONLY in the URL slug. The expired 07-15 twin was named 'Fareway 24 Pack Purified Drinking Water' at the same $3.87, so heal-degraded-sizes (keyed item+price) missed the rename.

trash-bags | Fareway | 'Bright Essentials Trash Bags, Black, Drawstring, Unscented, Large' | $7.88 | size='each' | slug '...-28-each'. Same shape: storage-bags 20-each, dryer-sheets 120-each, croissants 3-ct, tortillas 23-0-oz (=23.0), mangoes 12-oz. 61 rows in the file have size='each', 48 of them carry a size-bearing slug.

hand-soap | Fareway | 'Softsoap Liquid Hand Soap Pump, Fresh Breeze' | $1.99 | size='221 fl oz' vs slug '...-7-5-oz' (=7.5 fl oz) - a CORRUPTED size ~30x too big; per-unit $0.009/fl oz fell below band and the cell dropped. Same class: fruit-punch 'Hawaiian Punch Multi-serve Polar Blast' $3.48 size='512 fl oz' vs slug '1-gal' (=128 fl oz), 4x too big, band-dropped.

soda | Fareway | 'Pepsi Soda - Pack' | $9.49 | size='' | slug '...-pepsi-cola-12-fl-oz' names the PER-CAN size while the price is the PACK price - adopting the slug here would recreate the Aldi pack-price-vs-per-unit-size bug (2026-07-31-96ae4a). Same for 'Gatorade Frost, Glacier Cherry - Pack' (slug 20-fl-oz) and 'Shasta Cola, Diet' (slug 12-fl-oz).

SLUG DECIMAL LOSS: the slug encodes decimals as dashes ('15-25 oz' = 15.25) but sometimes drops the dot entirely: 'fareway-original-macaroni-cheese-dinner-725-oz' is a 7.25 oz box, not 725 oz. A naive slug parse would deflate per-unit 100x. Dashless 3+ digit weight tokens are ambiguous; counts (ct/each) have no decimals and are safe at any length.

Family Fare gaps: kale is IN family-fare-regular-2026-08-01.json at $1.79/lb but the kale commodity is unit=each, so the engine honestly refuses a per-lb row (board kale: Walmart 1.48 each etc.). feta candidates are premium 4 oz crumbles at $1.2475/oz vs the live row 0.30-0.745/oz (band refusal). brownie-mix / canned-green-beans / frozen-lasagna: only premium rows in the capture (Rao's lasagna 0.566/oz vs board 0.15-0.28) while the cheap search terms 'brownie mix', 'cut green beans can', 'frozen lasagna' sit in the file's 466-term empty_terms throttle ledger - the 3-hourly sweep self-heals these.

The rotisserie-chicken @ Fareway and onions @ Fareway gaps are audit FALSE CANDIDATES (Oscar Mayer rotisserie-seasoned LUNCH MEAT; a 6 oz diced-onion cup) - fixed as routing excludes in item 2026-08-01-08b14e, which removes them from the candidate pool.

surface_fix.what: derive the missing sizes from Fareway's own catalog slugs and re-emit the regular file, so the 14-day expiry stops taking sized rows with no sized successor
surface_fix.exact_change: extend the existing SLUG BASIS OVERRIDE (currently only '-1-lb'): when the row's size is 'each' or empty AND the item name does not end in '- Pack', parse the slug tail '-<num>-<unit>' where dashes inside <num> are decimal points. Adopt: any integer for ct/each units; dash-decimal or 1-2 digit dashless for oz/fl-oz/lb/gal. REFUSE dashless 3+ digit weight tokens (the 725-oz=7.25oz ambiguity) unless the NAME carries the same size. When a NON-empty captured size disagrees with the slug size by a factor of 1.5x or more, route the row to the existing basis-conflict drop path (the Softsoap 221-vs-7.5 and Hawaiian 512-vs-128 corruptions) instead of publishing either number.

items.root_cause: Three stacked mechanisms: (1) the Fareway storefront DOM extract reads a surface that does not carry the pack size for many products, so the builder writes size='each' or '' while the price is the pack price - the same surface-without-the-fact class as the Aldi product-page finding (2026-07-31-96ae4a); (2) heal-degraded-sizes keys on item+price, so a store RENAME ('Fareway 24 Pack Purified Drinking Water' -> 'Fareway Purified Drinking Water') defeats the heal even though the product id in the link_url (20544533) is identical; (3) the 14-day carry cap had been hiding this - on 07-31 it expired 196 old sized rows at once and every per-unit commodity whose only remaining Fareway row was size-less dropped off the board at the next comparison (08-01 06:10). The engine's refusal to price a size-less row is CORRECT and must stay.

root_fix.what: make the heal rename-proof and the slug the declared fallback surface
root_fix.exact_change: heal-degraded-sizes: match prior-capture rows by the numeric product id parsed from link_url (stable across renames) in addition to item+price, keeping the existing same-price guard. build-fareway-regular: the slug-size derivation from surface_fix, with a frozen self-test.

blast_radius.measured_by: all 554 deal rows of fareway-regular-2026-07-31.json (the newest Fareway regular file), plus coverage-gaps.json 15:23 and the board cells in comparison-2026-08-01.json
blast_radius.detail: 61 rows with size='each' + 4 with size=''. 48 of the 61 carry a size-bearing slug. Under the adoption rules: RECOVER with a safe count (ct/each slugs): bottled-water 24, trash-bags 28, storage-bags 20, dryer-sheets 120, dishwasher pacs 43, croissants 3. RECOVER with a safe weight (dash-decimal or short): tortillas 23.0 oz, mangoes 12 oz, lemons 16 oz (a bag; the engine and band then decide, refusal stays honest), microwave-popcorn 19.74 oz, granola-bars 10.91 oz, fruit-snacks 32 oz, hot-dog-buns 12.4 oz, instant-mashed-potatoes 6 oz (band-gated), plus the remaining non-gap rows. QUARANTINE as slug-vs-size conflict: hand-soap (Softsoap), fruit-punch (Hawaiian Punch) - absent by decision, visible in the conflict report. NOT RECOVERABLE (correctly): soda / sports-drinks '- Pack' rows (slug is per-unit), hamburger-buns 'sesame-yellow-hamburger-buns' (no size anywhere), mac-and-cheese '725-oz' ambiguity. Board risk: zero existing cells change; the change only ADDS Fareway cells to commodities that currently have none, every one at a price the store itself states, gated by the same bands.
blast_radius.risk: a wrongly adopted slug size would mint a wrong per-unit; contained by the pack-name refusal, the 3-digit-dashless refusal, the conflict quarantine, and the commodity bands downstream

items.resolution_note: 26 drops classified: 21 Fareway = the storefront sweep captures no pack size (size 'each' or empty) and the 14-day cap expired the 196 old sized rows on 07-31, so per-unit commodities lost their Fareway cells at the next compare. Fixed by deriving sizes from Fareway's own catalog slugs (dash-decimal aware, pack-suffix and ambiguity refusals, conflict quarantine for two corrupted-size rows) and making heal-degraded-sizes rename-proof via the link_url product id. 5 Family Fare = honest band/unit refusals of premium rows while the cheap terms sit in the throttle ledger; the 3-hourly sweep self-heals them. 2 gaps were audit false candidates, removed by the item-08b14e routing excludes.
items.premise_verified: TRUE, re-checked 2026-08-01 against fareway-regular-2026-07-31.json (still the newest Fareway file, built 07-31 11:52). carry_note reads "+105 carried ... 196 expired" verbatim. Every named evidence row reproduces exactly: bottled-water "Fareway Purified Drinking Water" $3.87 size="each" slug 24-each; trash-bags $7.88 slug 28-each (capture actually says "28 each"); hand-soap Softsoap $1.99 size="221 fl oz" vs slug 7-5-oz; fruit-punch Hawaiian Punch $3.48 size="512 fl oz" vs slug 1-gal; soda "Pepsi Soda - Pack" $9.49 size="" slug 12-fl-oz; mac-and-cheese slug 725-oz. TWO COUNTS DIFFER and neither changes the mechanism: size="" is 6 rows not 4 (67 size-less candidates, not 65), and coverage-gaps.json has moved from 26 gaps to 30 (Fareway still exactly 21; Family Fare 5 -> 7; plus 2 new Sam's Club) because the FF sweep re-ran at 16:56, which is the re-look the plan's own freshness line asks for.
items.deviation:
Seven deviations, all measured before acting.

1. THE PACK REFUSAL WAS TOO NARROW. exact_change refuses slug adoption when the name ends "- Pack", but the
plan''s own evidence names two rows that carry a single-serve fl-oz slug against a multipack price and do NOT
end in "- Pack": "Shasta Cola, Diet" ($4.98, slug 12-fl-oz) and "Gatorade Orange Thirst Quencher" ($8.48,
slug 20-fl-oz). Taking the slug there recreates the exact Aldi pack-price-as-unit-size bug the plan cites
(2026-07-31-96ae4a). Added a second refusal: a fl-oz/gal slug is adopted only when the NAME states the same
number. Measured cost on all four Fareway captures: ZERO legitimate rows lost (the only real fl-oz single,
Old Orchard 64 fl oz, already carries its own captured size and never reaches this path).

2. THE 1.5x CONFLICT RULE OVER-QUARANTINED 3x. Implemented literally it dropped SIX rows, not the two the
plan measured, and four were the SLUG being wrong about a correct capture: Glade air freshener (capture
7.3 oz vs slug "73-oz" - the decimal fell out); Fareway 2% milk (0.5 gal vs "05-gal"); Jimmy Dean sandwiches
(18 oz vs "4-5-oz", which is one of the "4 Count" the name states); Pero sugar snap peas (8 oz vs a stale
15-oz slug). Narrowed to the shape the plan actually documented - a CAPTURED size inflated far past the
catalog''s - with three ways out: a decimal-drop match, a pack-count reconciliation from the name, and a
direction test (a slug LARGER than the capture is a slug fault, not a corruption). Also added a leading-zero
refusal, since "05-gal" can only ever be half a gallon. Result: exactly the 2 quarantines the plan measured
(Softsoap, Hawaiian Punch), and the captured size - the surface the PRICE was read from - is no longer
deleted on the word of a source now caught being wrong in four distinct ways.

3. TWO LIVE WRONG PRICES FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME FILE (not a new class - build-fareway-regular.ps1
already documents this exact defect for its each-branch, fixed 2026-07-30; the gallon and dozen branches two
lines below were left with it). The canonical-unit relabel discarded a real captured size:
  milk @ Fareway  published $3.15 per GALLON for a "0.5 gal" capture (slug agrees: "05-gal").
                  True per-gallon $6.30. UNDERSTATED 2x, 4th cheapest of 7 on the milk row.
  eggs @ Fareway  published $2.17 per DOZEN for "Dutch Farms 18 Grade A Large Eggs" at $2.17 (slug "18-ct").
                  True per-dozen $1.45. OVERSTATED 1.5x, shown as the dearest eggs when it is 2nd cheapest.
Blast radius measured as CELLS: exactly 2, both re-priced, ZERO crowns moved (milk crown stays Aldi $3.00,
eggs crown stays Walmart $1.426). Both now carry frozen must-fire fixtures plus clean twins proving a row
with no usable volume/count still falls back to the old behaviour.

4. SLUG-COUNT FALLBACK FOR PER-ITEM COMMODITIES. A capture that states a WEIGHT on a unit=each commodity is
true and useless, so those rows published as "$5.99 each" for a bag. Measured across all four captures:
exactly 2 rows reach this branch, croissants (3 ct -> $2.00 each) and Sunbelt granola bars (10 ct -> $0.288
each), both on the plan''s own recovery list.

5. SIX OF THE PLAN''S WEIGHT RECOVERIES ARE NOT ACHIEVABLE, and that is correct. tortillas, mangoes, lemons,
microwave-popcorn, fruit-snacks and hot-dog-buns are unit=each commodities; a weight cannot divide into a
per-item price, so they keep "each" and stay band-refused. The plan''s own hedge ("the engine and band then
decide, refusal stays honest") covers this. instant-mashed-potatoes DID recover its 6 oz size and is then
band-refused at $0.832/oz, exactly as the plan predicted.

6. ONE UNPREDICTED SIZE CORRECTION, explained: Fareway string cheese moved 12 oz -> 10 oz. The 12 oz came
from a size-heal against a linkless 2026-07-14 row; the store''s own catalog slug for the product id the
current capture returns (103051939) says 10 oz. Per-unit rises $0.291 -> $0.349/oz, so the board had been
understating it.

7. THE NEVER-SHRINK GUARD FIRED, as the plan anticipated, and was not bypassed blind. Live file 554 rows vs
444 from a fresh build. Proved FIRST in an isolated scratch tree that the full chain (build -> carry-forward
-> size-heal) returns to 554 with ZERO rows lost, then used -Force on that evidence and re-verified the live
result against a backup: 554 rows, 0 lost, 0 gained, 11 changed, price_mode/mode_verified preserved.

BOARD RESULT: 6 of the 21 Fareway gaps closed and live (bottled-water $0.1612, trash-bags $0.2814,
storage-bags $0.114, dryer-sheets $0.0328, croissants $1.9967, granola-bars $0.288); 2 quarantined by
decision and named in the builder report (hand-soap, fruit-punch); 2 were audit false candidates removed by
item 08b14e; the rest are honest band or unit refusals. No crown moved anywhere.

items.root_cause: Seven wrong-product classes the rule library cannot express, each proven by more names than the one that alerted: (a) flavor-carrier snacks - 'sour cream & onion' names 9 chips products that all reach the sour-cream commodity; (b) modifier-phrase sugar claims - 'lower/reduced/less sugar' names 7 products (Gatorade x2, Craisins x3, Quaker oatmeal, a ketchup) that all reach the sugar commodity because its excludes only cover no/zero/added; (c) granulated spices vs fresh produce - 7 names; (d) rotisserie-SEASONED lunch meat vs the rotisserie-chicken each-commodity - 8 names; (e) dressing/marinade carriers on produce and nuts, which also BLOCK bottled-marinade from names it should own - 6 names; (f) snack kits and personal-care 'butter' - 5 names; (g) a baby-food brand outside the brand list - 10 names. Where these tokens are estate-wide classes they belong in the category-excludes library so the bake applies them everywhere, not only where today's names happened to land.

root_fix.what: add the class tokens at the library level and re-bake, so the classes are closed estate-wide instead of patched per-commodity
root_fix.exact_change: put (a) flavor-carrier chips, (b) the lower/reduced/less-sugar modifier, (e) vinaigrette/marinade-carrier, (f) shea/hand-wash personal care, and (g) 'serenity\s*kids' into the appropriate category-excludes classes for produce/dairy/pantry categories; run the apply-category-excludes re-bake until -WhatIf reports +0 (the 07-31 lesson: an unbaked library silently drifts). The purely local tokens (granulated on garlic/onions, broth on mushrooms, crackers on cream-cheese, cherubs, lunch meat, balanced breaks, lean cuisine, diced) stay commodity-level.

items.deviation:
